summary: C1.3 is the torus/waveguide DSP-theory cluster — already one of the most densely self-linked neighborhoods in the palace (Dissolutions holds seven members by member-of alone, and 2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer has 28 inbound). The folders are not blind to much inside the room; almost every plausible internal pairing is already typed, often correctly as mirrors/couples-with rather than the lazier connects-to. What the community cut actually surfaced was outside the room: two newcomers this cluster should be reaching for. control-vocabulary-math (zero inbound, Neural Granular Synthesis project) formalizes the Kuramoto order parameter r and critical coupling K_c as a performable control surface for a spiking-neuron population — which is a literal, worked answer to the "invent control vocabularies for high-dimensional instrument spaces" problem that Infeasible DSP Now Shippable and Rank-N Lattice Analysis both name and leave open, and it shares its synchronization-bifurcation math with the Kuramoto type-3 warp Three Kinds of Warp formalizes for the torus. And Synthesis Topologies — thin, seed-stage, easy to overlook — turns out to share its exact "fixed-skeleton-variable-flesh" framing with the newcomer ControlNet as Topology's "armature" language, one audio, one image-diffusion, same underlying move. Inside the room, the one genuine new find was structural rather than cross-domain: Dissolutions' own forward vector wonders whether it needs a "Refusals" sibling — entries that look mergeable but structurally aren't — and Three Kinds of Warp's 1D obstruction theorem (no amount of clever type-1 warping ever produces inharmonicity) is exactly that case, sitting right next to Dissolutions with no link between them.

typed_relations.label: worked-control-vocabulary
typed_relations.rationale: Infeasible DSP Now Shippable names 'control-surface design is the hardest problem in the suite' and its own Forward Vectors say 'invent control vocabularies for high-dimensional instrument spaces — the concrete form of the hardest problem.' control-vocabulary-math is a worked instance of exactly that: it collapses a 16-64-neuron Kuramoto population into four performable knobs (K, sigma_threshold, frequency spread, drive) with r as the single closing-the-loop readout.
typed_relations.evidence: Infeasible DSP Now Shippable: 'control-surface design is the hardest problem in the suite... Invent control vocabularies for high-dimensional instrument spaces — the concrete form of the hardest problem.' control-vocabulary-math: 'This document formalizes the layer that sits on top of that engine: the statistical descriptors that turn a noisy crowd of N spiking neurons into four or five smooth, performable knobs.'

typed_relations.label: sync-bifurcation-as-knob
typed_relations.rationale: Both formalize the Kuramoto synchronization threshold as a designed musical control, not just a physics fact — one on a torus's two phasors, one on a population of spiking neurons. control-vocabulary-math's K_c ('below it the crowd drifts, above it synchrony switches on') is the same object as Three Kinds of Warp's type-3 lock/drift bifurcation ('a snap, not a fade'), same math, different material.
typed_relations.evidence: control-vocabulary-math: 'The critical coupling K_c is the threshold where r lifts off zero — below it the crowd drifts, above it synchrony switches on.' Three Kinds of Warp: 'Below the synchronization threshold the rotation numbers shift... above threshold they lock... Bends the lattice itself... The Kuramoto coupling f1 = K sin(phi2-phi1) is the canonical instance.'
typed_relations.fidelity_test: Swapped against DSP in Looping Dimensions (also names a Kuramoto bifurcation) — the reason still reads true there too, but Three Kinds of Warp is the room member that formalizes the type-3 typology with the explicit lock/drift language control-vocabulary-math's K_c matches most precisely, so it is the sharper target; kept both as candidates but chose the tighter one to avoid link-spreading a single newcomer across the whole cluster.

typed_relations.label: fixed-skeleton-free-surface
typed_relations.rationale: Synthesis Topologies names 'fixed-skeleton-variable-flesh designs (2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer's seven surfaces)' as one of its topology in-betweens. ControlNet as Topology names ControlNet itself as 'an armature... the wire skeleton a figure is built around — it fixes the pose before a single detail exists.' Same organizing move — a fixed structural skeleton constrains a free surface of variation — in two completely different domains (audio synth architecture, diffusion-model conditioning).
typed_relations.evidence: Synthesis Topologies: 'Fixed-skeleton-variable-flesh designs (2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer's seven surfaces).' ControlNet as Topology: 'ControlNet is an armature. In clay modeling the armature is the wire skeleton a figure is built around — it fixes the pose before a single detail exists.'
typed_relations.fidelity_test: Swapped against Torus Warping Catalog or DSP in Looping Dimensions — neither carries the fixed-skeleton/free-surface language; the rhyme is specific to these two entries' own vocabulary, not generic.

typed_relations.label: resists-dissolution
typed_relations.rationale: Dissolutions' own Forward Vectors ask whether it needs a 'Refusals' sibling — 'entries that resist dissolution despite looking like they should merge.' Three Kinds of Warp's 1D obstruction theorem is exactly that structural refusal: no amount of clever type-1 phase reshaping (the move every commercial wavetable warp makes) can ever become type-2 or type-3 and produce inharmonicity — two things that look mergeable (more sophisticated warping = eventually inharmonic) and provably are not.
typed_relations.evidence: Dissolutions: 'Does the catalogue eventually grow a sibling — Refusals, the entries that resist dissolution despite looking like they should merge? Two things that keep being mistaken for one and shouldn't be?' Three Kinds of Warp: 'The theorem holds for any warp at all... Every commercial wavetable warp redistributes energy among the harmonic slots; none of them moves a partial between slots... Structurally cannot produce inharmonicity.'
